title: SCLATE: A Substrate for Continual-Learning Agent Training and Evaluation
gist: Apple researchers present SCLATE, an event-scheduling execution substrate with a hybrid simulated clock that lets unmodified agent harnesses and memory systems be benchmarked and post-trained over month-long multi-session scenarios compressed into hours. Head-to-head tests across ten models find add-on memory systems do not reliably beat native harness memory, and post-training Qwen3.5-4B through unmodified harnesses yields 6.8x fewer file lines read and +16.7 points on SWE-bench Verified.

insights.claim: Continual-learning agents are best understood as systems of models, harnesses, and memory operating over long multi-session horizons, not as standalone models.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Agent value accrues to the full stack (harness + memory + model), widening the competitive surface beyond model labs.
insights.quote: Continual-learning agents are systems of models, harnesses, and memory operating over long multi-session horizons.
insights.locator: Continual-learning agents are systems of models

insights.claim: Existing agent benchmarks and training frameworks only schedule their own events, forcing every benchmark-agent pairing to build a custom scheduling loop for agent-side events like session stop/start, crons, and memory consolidation.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Evaluation tooling for long-horizon agents is immature, a gap for infra/tooling vendors and a reason to distrust current agent leaderboards.
insights.quote: existing benchmarks and training frameworks schedule only the benchmark’s own events, leaving each benchmark and agent pair to build a custom scheduling loop
insights.locator: Continual-learning agents are systems of models

insights.claim: SCLATE uses a single open event scheduler to which benchmarks and unmodified agents each add events via an adapter, plus a hybrid simulated clock that runs in real time while the agent works and skips idle gaps, compressing a month-long scenario into hours.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Time compression makes long-horizon agent evaluation and RL rollouts economically feasible, lowering cost of iterating on persistent agents.
insights.quote: compresses a month-long scenario into hours
insights.locator: We present SCLATE, an execution substrate

insights.claim: SCLATE doubles as a rollout engine that runs any agent's harness and memory unmodified and records tokens and log probabilities of every model call via an in-container proxy, enabling RL post-training through real production harnesses.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Training models inside the exact harnesses they will be deployed in is a moat-building technique for vertically integrated agent products.
insights.quote: recording the tokens and log probabilities of every model call through an in-container proxy
insights.locator: SCLATE also serves as a rollout engine

themes.theme: Memory systems vs native harness memory

insights.claim: Across seven ported benchmarks, ten harness/memory configurations, and ten models, adding a dedicated memory system did not reliably outperform the harness's native memory.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Skepticism warranted toward standalone agent-memory startups whose products bolt onto existing harnesses.

insights.claim: Models differ widely in how effectively they use the same harness and memory configuration, so harness/memory choice and model choice interact rather than being independent.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Model benchmark rankings may not transfer across agent stacks; co-optimization of model and harness is a differentiator.
insights.quote: models differ widely in how they use the same harness and memory

insights.claim: Post-training Qwen3.5-4B through unmodified harnesses and memory systems taught it to read 6.8x fewer file lines while raising its SWE-bench Verified pass rate by 16.7 points.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Harness-aware RL can make small (on-device-scale) models both cheaper in context usage and more capable at coding agents.
insights.quote: reading 6.8× fewer file lines with a 16.7-point higher SWE-bench Verified pass rate

insights.claim: The post-trained Qwen3.5-4B wrote richer memory records and its held-out MetaClaw accuracy rose by up to 11.8 points, suggesting learned memory use generalizes beyond training tasks.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Memory-use skill is trainable into small models, relevant to Apple's on-device personal-agent ambitions.
insights.quote: its held-out MetaClaw accuracy rises by up to 11.8 points

insights.claim: Apple researchers chose an open-weight Chinese model family (Qwen) as the base for agent post-training experiments.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Signals Qwen's entrenchment as the default open small-model base even inside US big tech research.
